XXBxV6-zamM.summary: Micro Men is a 2009 BBC comic drama about the early 1980s British home computer boom. It follows the rivalry between Clive Sinclair and Acorn founder Chris Curry over the BBC Micro contract and the ZX Spectrum.
XXBxV6-zamM.why: HN recommends it often as an entertaining and authentic dramatization of Sinclair versus Acorn, the story from which ARM grew.

XetplHcM7aQ.summary: The first episode of James Burke's 1978 BBC series Connections traces modern dependence on complex technological networks, starting with the 1965 New York blackout, and moves through ancient agriculture to Kuwait's oil-driven leap.
XetplHcM7aQ.why: Heavily recommended as a masterpiece of popular science and the classic illustration of how fragile interdependent systems are, trotted out in every blackout or supply chain thread.

XA2WjJbmmoM.summary: A thoughtbot meetup talk by Max Cantor on getting most of what popular plugins provide using only built-in Vim features. It covers autocomplete, file jumping, filesystem navigation, build integration and snippets, with slides and a vimrc available.
XA2WjJbmmoM.why: HN treats it as the canonical talk for the case that vanilla Vim goes a long way and plugin dependencies are a burden.

XuBdf9jYj7o.summary: A short BicycleDutch video on how the Netherlands got its cycling infrastructure, including the 1970s protests and the shift away from car-centric planning. The channel later published an updated version.
XuBdf9jYj7o.why: HN uses it as the standard short answer to whether car-dominated cities can become bike-friendly, since the Dutch had to fight for it.

XZ3w_jec1v8.summary: Evan Czaplicki, creator of Elm, examines how programming languages are funded. He looks at where compiler engineers' salaries come from, why Go has about 5 engineers while Dart has about 30, and how this limits language design.
XZ3w_jec1v8.why: Recommended repeatedly as a funny, informative talk on the economics behind programming languages and open source.

X2wLP0izeJE.summary: A five-minute clip of Ira Glass on the gap between good taste and early creative work. He says beginners know their work falls short and must keep producing to close the gap.
X2wLP0izeJE.why: HN commenters return to it as motivation for creators who feel their work is not good enough yet.

XheAMrS8Q1c.summary: Biologist Michael Levin explains the bioelectric layer that coordinates cells to build organs and bodies, showing footage of two-headed worms and introducing xenobots. He discusses implications for medicine and the nature of life.
XheAMrS8Q1c.why: HN commenters use it as the accessible 20-minute entry point to Levin's bioelectricity research whenever regeneration or cell signaling comes up.

X-iSQQgOd1A.summary: Sebastian Lague explores an ant-inspired algorithm and simulates ant and slime mold behavior, using compute shaders. Source code for both simulations is available.
X-iSQQgOd1A.why: HN recommends it as a beautiful example of what simple rules and compute shaders can produce, and many commenters were inspired by it.

XVbuk3jizGM.summary: Matthaeus Krenn presents a concept for car touchscreen UI where the screen controls only one thing at a time, designed to suit driving. A tablet prototype accompanies the short demo.
XVbuk3jizGM.why: Repeatedly cited in car touchscreen debates as an elegant, sensible alternative to distracting automotive UIs.

XEVlyP4_11M.summary: John Oliver interviews Edward Snowden about NSA surveillance, including street interviews showing people have not thought about what the government can see. The segment famously frames the issue through private photos.
XEVlyP4_11M.why: HN points to it as the best way to explain to ordinary people why privacy and mass surveillance matter.

XFDM1ip5HdU.summary: 3Blue1Brown explores infinite sums from convergent to divergent, with an introduction to the 2-adic metric, themed on the cycle between discovering and inventing mathematics.
XFDM1ip5HdU.why: Recommended as a favorite Grant Sanderson video and a visual introduction to p-adic numbers and sums like 1+2+4+...

XGo4PJd1lng.summary: Tantacrul explains how he and engraver Simon Smith designed the free music notation font for MuseScore 3.6. It draws on the history of the SCORE notation application by Leland Smith.
XGo4PJd1lng.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining look at how hard notation fonts are to make, and it comes up in threads on music engraving and open source.

XfQUOHlAocY.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how many American suburbs, built all at once rather than incrementally, cannot cover their infrastructure costs and survive on growing debt. It draws on Strong Towns' work on the growth Ponzi scheme.
XfQUOHlAocY.why: Recommended as an introduction to the finances of suburban sprawl and its long-term consequences.

XI5frPV58tY.summary: Mycologist Paul Stamets presents six ways mycelium and fungi could help save the world, in an 18-minute TED talk. Topics include environmental cleanup and other applications of fungi.
XI5frPV58tY.why: Recommended as an engaging, down-to-earth talk on the world-changing potential of fungi.

XRr1kaXKBsU.summary: Veritasium explains, with expert input, that in general relativity gravity is not a force and objects follow straight paths through curved spacetime, including why standing on the ground means you are accelerating.
XRr1kaXKBsU.why: HN links it as a go-to intuitive explanation whenever gravity as spacetime curvature or free fall comes up.

XvDZLjaCJuw.summary: A 1982 AT&T Bell Labs film for students about the Unix system and how it can be used practically. It includes Lorinda Cherry building a talking calculator by piping together Unix commands, and a spell checker made from Unix utilities.
XvDZLjaCJuw.why: HN commenters recommend it as a demonstration of the Unix philosophy, with small tools composed through pipes.

XRYN2xt11Ek.summary: A Netflix JavaScript talk on using Reactive Extensions (Rx) for asynchronous UI code. It covers Observables, composing events such as drag and drop, and sequencing Ajax requests.
XRYN2xt11Ek.why: Recommended as a clear, mind-changing introduction to observables and async programming from engineers using Rx in production.

XfcvX0P1b5g.summary: Barely Sociable presents a case that Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto is cryptographer Adam Back. It uses interview clips and circumstantial evidence, and also touches on the block size dispute.
XfcvX0P1b5g.why: HN commenters recommend it as a compelling, if not definitive, argument for Adam Back as Satoshi whenever the identity question comes up.

XpDsk374LDE.summary: Elm creator Evan Czaplicki's talk on how a file grows and when to split code up. He argues for keeping code in one file until it hurts and warns against premature extraction.
XpDsk374LDE.why: Recommended as the argument for code colocation and delaying abstraction.

X1XoCQm5JSQ.summary: In this American Masters clip, Jacques Pepin shows two different techniques for making a perfect omelet, a dish he is famous for teaching America.
X1XoCQm5JSQ.why: HN people call it a favorite cooking video and a model of mastery, showing two omelet styles in about five minutes.

X8jsijhllIA.summary: 3Blue1Brown's discovery-oriented introduction to error correction codes, building up Hamming codes from the puzzle of locating a flipped bit. It explains the parity-check idea and why it is so efficient.
X8jsijhllIA.why: HN recommends it as an invaluable, intuitive explanation of Hamming codes that pairs well with hardware-oriented treatments.

XDM3MqHln8U.summary: A 29C3 panel with whistleblowers Jesselyn Radack, Thomas Drake and William Binney. They talk about what happens when exposing secret government power becomes a crime, and about surveillance abuses.
XDM3MqHln8U.why: Recommended as a first-hand account from NSA whistleblowers, often linked in surveillance and Snowden threads.

XUT8ec24anM.summary: An Onion News Network sketch in which two teenage girls appear on TV to plead for their kidnapped friend's release, then start gossiping about classmates. It is a satirical parody of teen behavior and sensational news.
XUT8ec24anM.why: HN commenters call it one of the best and funniest Onion News Network videos and a sharp parody of teen girls.

XKu_SEDAykw.summary: Two Google engineers perform a mock coding interview and then discuss best practices for candidates, including asking clarifying questions and communicating while solving.
XKu_SEDAykw.why: Cited as a realistic, well-run example of a technical interview, both for candidates preparing and interviewers calibrating.

XTeJ64KD5cg.summary: Numberphile's Tony Padilla and Matt Parker discuss Graham's number, once the largest number used in a mathematical proof, and how enormous it is.
XTeJ64KD5cg.why: Recommended as the mind-melting intro to unimaginably large numbers.

XOR8mk0tLpc.summary: A scene from the TV drama Halt and Catch Fire in which Gordon Clark meets Joe MacMillan, who is posing as an IBM salesman, on a sales call. It includes the dialogue about IBM being the safe choice and a marketing guru telling an engineer when to stop talking.
XOR8mk0tLpc.why: HN commenters post it as a favorite scene about IBM's reputation and sales psychology.

X9RYuvPCQUA.summary: Kirby Ferguson's updated four-part video essay arguing that creativity is built on copying, transforming and combining existing work. It covers examples from film, music and technology and touches on generative AI.
X9RYuvPCQUA.why: Pointed to in copyright and AI debates as a compelling case that all culture is remix.

XH0F9r0siTI.summary: Christopher Domas's DEF CON 26 talk on secret processor registers that vendors reserve for third parties holding trusted keys. He examines how users are locked out of parts of their own CPUs.
XH0F9r0siTI.why: HN commenters call his x86 internals talks spectacular and mention them whenever low-level processor surprises come up.

XJ97iXQrqzw.summary: An episode of Plogue's chipresearch series on emulating the Yamaha DX7 from the hardware up. It covers the sub CPU and main CPU, address map investigation, cartridges, firmware analysis and a skeleton MAME driver.
XJ97iXQrqzw.why: Recommended in DX7 reverse-engineering threads as a look at the effort behind bit-accurate emulation.

XJ9ckqCMiKk.summary: A joint Erlang Factory 2016 keynote by Phoenix creator Chris McCord and Elm creator Evan Czaplicki on using the two together, including Phoenix.Presence design and PubSub optimizations.
XJ9ckqCMiKk.why: Pointed to as the best source on Phoenix Presence internals and for combining Phoenix with Elm.

XVmsfL5LG90.summary: British Museum curator Irving Finkel teaches how to write cuneiform, with a colleague following along. It is a short, lively introduction to the script.
XVmsfL5LG90.why: Recommended as the best short, funny and approachable introduction to cuneiform on YouTube.

Xe5AE-qYan8.summary: A 57-minute account of Clifford Stoll's tracking of a KGB-linked hacker through Lawrence Berkeley Lab computers in 1986, the story of The Cuckoo's Egg. It covers the FBI and Chaos Computer Club involvement.
Xe5AE-qYan8.why: Recommended as a documentary telling the early hacking and spy-hunting story, with the original people involved.

XuKjBIBBAL8.summary: A three-minute clip from BBC's Planet Earth narrated by David Attenborough about Cordyceps, the fungus that infects insects and takes over their behavior. It shows an infected ant and its demise.
XuKjBIBBAL8.why: HN links it as the quick introduction to zombie-ant fungi whenever the topic comes up.

XusyNT_k-1c.summary: A Climate Town episode on who uses America's water, particularly Western water. It looks at agriculture such as alfalfa and animal feed, and at water-rights rules that discourage conservation.
XusyNT_k-1c.why: HN points to it in Colorado River and water-use threads as an accessible explainer of why the Western water shortage keeps getting worse.

XxCha4Kez9c.summary: Tom Scott visits the USPS Remote Encoding Center in Salt Lake City, where keyers decipher mail images machines cannot read. It shows the lengths taken to decode bad handwriting.
XxCha4Kez9c.why: Recommended in address and OCR threads as a look at the last human mail-coding operation.

X1T3IQ4N-3g.summary: CppCon 2014 talk by Jeff Preshing on how Ubisoft Montreal developed games for multicore hardware, before and after C++11 concurrency support. It goes into atomics and lock-free programming in practice.
X1T3IQ4N-3g.why: Recommended as a clear, practical introduction to atomics and lock-free programming in C++.

X29lF43mUlo.summary: A clip from George Carlin's "You Are All Diseased" special in which he riffs on germs, the immune system and white blood cells. It argues that modern obsession with cleanliness is misplaced.
X29lF43mUlo.why: HN brings it up as comic relief and as a funny take when immunity, dirt and germs come up.

XtMmeAjQTXc.summary: The first episode of Caltech's The Mechanical Universe, a 52-part introductory university physics series. David Goodstein introduces ideas from Copernicus to Newton, linking the physics of the heavens and the earth with computer animation.
XtMmeAjQTXc.why: HN rates the series as one of the best physics lecture courses on YouTube, with an engaging format and historical context.

X4Neivqp2K4.summary: Seventeen-year-old Ray Kurzweil appears on the TV show I've Got a Secret in 1965, playing a piece of music composed by a computer program he built.
X4Neivqp2K4.why: HN shares it as an impressive early example of computer-generated music and of Kurzweil's precocity.

X6NJkWbM1xk.summary: Tom Scott recounts the worst typo he ever made, a subtle mistake in code with destructive consequences at a previous job. It is a cautionary tale about irreversible operations.
X6NJkWbM1xk.why: Shared in outage and accidental-deletion threads as a relatable, well-told horror story.

X8aWBcPVPMo.summary: A one-minute clip from Richard Feynman's 1979 Auckland lecture in which he answers whether you see an object or only its light. It is a short, playful take on perception and on the use of philosophy.
X8aWBcPVPMo.why: HN uses it to illustrate Feynman's wry view of philosophical questions and perception.

XO9FKQAxWZc.summary: Nina Paley's TEDxMaastricht talk arguing against copyright and for copyleft and free culture. She argues that restricting ideas harms creativity and that culture belongs to everyone.
XO9FKQAxWZc.why: Brought up in copyright, public domain and AI-training debates as a provocative argument for abolishing copyright.

XRAP3lBivYM.summary: Emery Berger's CppCon 2019 talk introducing Mesh, a drop-in malloc replacement that compacts memory in unmodified C and C++ programs. It tackles fragmentation by merging pages without changing pointers.
XRAP3lBivYM.why: HN recommends Berger's talks as fascinating and cites Mesh as mind-blowing memory allocator work.

XRXwWbo_mX0.summary: A short clip of a Renault F1 engine playing God Save the Queen by precisely controlling its RPM, recorded at Goodwood. It demonstrates how finely the drivetrain can be controlled.
XRXwWbo_mX0.why: Treated as a favorite hack and a go-to example in threads about machines playing music.

XSoOrlh5i1k.summary: A recorded phone call in which the Lenny bot, a looping set of prerecorded replies from a rambling old man, keeps a telemarketer on the line for 14 minutes. The uploader calls it the best Lenny call yet.
XSoOrlh5i1k.why: HN mentions it as an example of Lenny, the telemarketer time-waster, and of how a canned script can fool callers for a long time.

XeJSXfXep4M.summary: David Rock gives a Google Tech Talk based on his book Your Brain at Work, using neuroscience to explain why focus and productivity are hard at the office. He gives strategies for managing mental energy and distraction.
XeJSXfXep4M.why: HN commenters point to it as a general overview of the cognitive science of insight and focus that is useful for developers and knowledge workers.

XehNK7UpZsc.summary: A video essay arguing that the next major real-time strategy game will fail unless it gets the fundamentals right. It covers the playerbase and demographics, what older RTS games did well, and the roles of the engine, spectacle, development tools and player-generated content.
XehNK7UpZsc.why: HN recommends it for its argument that single-player campaigns and modding are overlooked in RTS design.

XgRlrBl-7Yg.summary: In this TED talk, Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman distinguishes the experiencing self from the remembering self, using examples such as vacations and colonoscopies. He explains how the two perceive happiness differently and what that means for economics, policy and self-awareness.
XgRlrBl-7Yg.why: HN commenters recommend it in threads on happiness and well-being as a clear account of why memory and experience of happiness diverge.

XopSDJq6w8E.summary: The ADVChina hosts tour a villa neighborhood in southern China that was built only three years earlier and is already empty and deteriorating. They use it to discuss ghost cities, building quality and the real estate bubble.
XopSDJq6w8E.why: HN commenters cite it in threads on China's housing glut and construction quality as visual evidence of poor, empty new buildings.

XwRSS7jeo5s.summary: A one-minute clip of Jacob Collier tuning a piano, remarking that it is not in tune at all. It touches on his views on equal temperament and tuning.
XwRSS7jeo5s.why: Used as an example in music theory and tuning discussions of continuous-pitch thinking beyond equal temperament.

X3NASGb5m8s.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs explaining why Xerox failed, arguing that product people lose out to sales and marketing people once a company becomes dominant.
X3NASGb5m8s.why: HN cites it as the standard explanation of how finance and sales take over a company, applied to Boeing and other declining firms.

XBmJay_qdNc.summary: An RSA Animate adaptation of a Dan Ariely lecture on dishonesty. It explores when ordinary people lie or cheat and how they rationalize small acts of dishonesty.
XBmJay_qdNc.why: HN cites it for Ariely's finding that people cheat a little without feeling guilty.

XRrLyckg8Nc.summary: A 2012 debate between Peter Thiel and George Gilder on whether technological progress and economic growth are accelerating or decelerating, moderated by William Davidow.
XRrLyckg8Nc.why: Cited for Thiel's technological stagnation thesis, especially his argument that energy costs offset IT productivity gains.

XZGiVzIr8Qg.summary: A 1983 interview clip in which David Bowie questions MTV VJ Mark Goodman about why the channel played so few videos by black artists.
XZGiVzIr8Qg.why: Cited as a famous, pointed example of Bowie challenging MTV's exclusion of black music, in threads on media gatekeeping.

XnRCZK3KjUY.summary: A 72-hour timelapse of Reddit's 2017 April Fools' experiment r/place, a collaborative pixel canvas where each user could place one pixel every few minutes. The frames come from an image archive and the Reddit API.
XnRCZK3KjUY.why: HN commenters link it as the full record of r/place whenever the experiment, or collaborative canvases in general, comes up.

X0VH78ye4yY.summary: An F8 2015 talk touring the tool-chain Facebook uses to let thousands of engineers build mobile apps, including its move to Mercurial, an Atom-based IDE and continuous integration.
X0VH78ye4yY.why: HN points to it as a look at developer infrastructure at large scale, with speakers covering source control and CI test selection.

X36ye-1x_HQ.summary: Edwin Brady, creator of Idris, introduces type-driven development in a dependently typed language. He shows types being written first and programs derived with interactive editing, then extends beyond simple examples to programs that interact with users and networks.
X36ye-1x_HQ.why: HN points to it as a demonstration of type-directed editing with typed holes, which some see as a likely future of programming.

XCvwCcEP74Q.summary: Scott Galloway's DLD15 talk assessing the competitive positions of Amazon, Apple, Facebook and Google. He argues about where each is strong and weak, including Amazon's need for physical retail.
XCvwCcEP74Q.why: Shared in 2015 threads as an insightful framework for strategic moves by the big tech companies.

XFJnWp1tAdU.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explains how a US Navy nuclear submarine surfaces through Arctic ice, filmed during the ICEx exercise. It shows ballast and control systems and the physics involved.
XFJnWp1tAdU.why: HN points to it as the best accessible explanation of submarine ice breaking and sub controls.

XGbPHp6QfkQ.summary: Jason Cammisa reviews the 2022 Volkswagen Mk8 GTI and explains why he thinks it is worse than the Mk7. He criticizes aspects such as the capacitive touch controls and the interface.
XGbPHp6QfkQ.why: HN cites it in threads on touchscreens versus physical buttons in cars, as an example of an enthusiast's critique of VW's UX.

XTl7Jn_kmio.summary: Matthias Felleisen's keynote uses weather prediction as an analogy for type systems, arguing they forecast problems so you can act on them. It draws on his experience developing Typed Racket.
XTl7Jn_kmio.why: Referenced in static versus dynamic typing debates, including his remark that Hindley-Milner doesn't really work.

XVv1GipR5yU.summary: A JuliaCon 2016 talk by Shashi Gowda showing an APL implementation in Julia. APL code is translated to Julia and JIT compiled to machine code.
XVv1GipR5yU.why: Cited in APL and Julia threads as a neat way to run APL-style syntax at Julia's speed.

XZJc1p6RE78.summary: Computerphile video in which Mike Pound explains a University of Maryland paper on watermarking LLM output. The method biases token choices so generated text can later be detected statistically.
XZJc1p6RE78.why: Linked as the approachable explanation whenever HN discusses detecting or watermarking AI-generated text.

X_tYrnv_o6A.summary: Veritasium short showing Drew Berry's scientifically accurate animations of the molecular machines that drive cell division. It walks through mitosis, chromosomes and motor proteins.
X_tYrnv_o6A.why: Cited as an easy-to-digest look at the awe-inspiring animations of cellular machinery.

Xe1a1wHxTyo.summary: The Monty Python sketch in which four wealthy Yorkshiremen try to outdo each other with exaggerated tales of childhood poverty.
Xe1a1wHxTyo.why: HN mostly posts it as a joke whenever someone says things were harder in the old days.

Xe1g1JrRRkY.summary: A Fully Charged episode on Electroflight, an early-stage project to build a fully electric racing plane that can exceed 300 mph. It features two motors driving contra-rotating propellers.
Xe1g1JrRRkY.why: HN points to it in electric aviation threads for how small electric motors enable contra-rotating props.

XgFbqSYdNK4.summary: A four-minute 2006 explainer on trusted computing, describing what it is and whether users should support it, with a skeptical DRM angle.
XgFbqSYdNK4.why: Cited as an easy-to-understand framing of trusted computing and TPMs as tools that can treat users as threats.

XkDEzfpdcSg.summary: Kate Gregory's CppCon 2017 talk picks ten highlights from the C++ Core Guidelines and shows examples and benefits for each. It is aimed at C++ developers of any experience level who have not read the full guidelines.
XkDEzfpdcSg.why: Recommended as the condensed tl;dr of the C++ Core Guidelines and as a route into modern C++.

XpQMgbDJPok.summary: A five-minute BicycleDutch episode showing how Dutch junctions are designed so cyclists and pedestrians can cross safely. It explains the layout choices that separate and protect them.
XpQMgbDJPok.why: Recommended as a short, comprehensive look at Dutch junction design, often cited when discussing intersections as a solved problem.

XvwNKpDUkiE.summary: Professor Brailsford of the University of Nottingham describes how the university set out to print its own mathematics exam papers in the 1980s. The story centers on getting a Mergenthaler Linotron 202 typesetter to work with their own software.
XvwNKpDUkiE.why: HN commenters point to it as the history of phototypesetters and a story about the freedom to control your own hardware.

XyJh3qKjSMk.summary: A two-minute Yes Prime Minister scene in which Sir Humphrey persuades Jim Hacker to buy Trident, using tortured logic about nuclear deterrence.
XyJh3qKjSMk.why: HN mostly quotes it as a joke about the nuclear missile Harrods would sell, and one commenter praises the show as political education.

XziuEdpVUe0.summary: Planets is a track from the audiovisual album Oscilloscope Music, in which the audio signal drives an analog oscilloscope directly. The left channel sets horizontal deflection and the right sets vertical, so the sound draws vector graphics.
XziuEdpVUe0.why: HN cites it as the example of oscilloscope music, where the song itself is the visual, in XY mode.

X2fGzmphx4U.summary: Press conference footage in which the suspects in the 2007 Boston Mooninite bomb scare answer questions about 1960s and 1970s hairstyles.
X2fGzmphx4U.why: HN uses it as a joke about the absurdity of the Mooninite panic, and one commenter who attended shared it.

X3-hOigoxHs.summary: A video essay from Pop Culture Detective arguing that The Big Bang Theory normalizes sexism and toxic masculinity through its portrayal of nerd men. It analyzes recurring tropes in how the male leads treat women.
X3-hOigoxHs.why: Cited as a critique whenever HN discusses the show's depiction of nerd culture and STEM men.

X5REM-3nWHg.summary: A short Conan segment in which George R. R. Martin explains that he writes his Game of Thrones books on WordStar 4.0 on a DOS machine.
X5REM-3nWHg.why: Cited as the standard example of a famous writer who prefers an old, distraction-free DOS word processor.

X7HmltUWXgs.summary: A one-minute Rick and Morty clip in which a small robot asks its purpose and learns it is to pass butter.
X7HmltUWXgs.why: Used purely as a joke reference when discussing robots, AI or pointless tasks.

X8XZriAdB1g.summary: Half as Interesting explains why airlines flew empty 'ghost flights' out of Heathrow to keep their landing slots under use-it-or-lose-it rules.
X8XZriAdB1g.why: Cited to show that empty slot-keeping flights predate COVID and Lufthansa's recent practice.

XAeEpbtHDPw.summary: A one-minute clip from HBO's Silicon Valley in which Gavin Belson comments on sycophants. It satirizes executives surrounded by yes-men.
XAeEpbtHDPw.why: Mostly used as a joking or illustrative reference when threads cover yes-men, executive hubris and sycophancy.

XAfTXYa36f4.summary: A short excerpt from the 2007 iPhone launch where Steve Jobs quotes Alan Kay: people serious about software should make their own hardware. It explains part of why Apple built the phone itself.
XAfTXYa36f4.why: Cited whenever HN discusses Apple's vertical integration and its custom silicon.

XEL65gywwHQ.summary: A one-minute Seinfeld clip where Kramer explains that the post office will pay for Jerry's broken stereo because of a tax write-off.
XEL65gywwHQ.why: Posted as a joke whenever someone misunderstands what a tax write-off actually means.

XGK84Poeynk.summary: A Symphony of Science music video that auto-tunes samples of Carl Sagan, Richard Feynman, Neil deGrasse Tyson and Bill Nye into a song about the wonder of the universe.
XGK84Poeynk.why: Linked casually as a fitting companion when threads turn to awe at the universe.

XIaovi1JWyY.summary: Footage of Airbus's 2006 certification evacuation trial of the A380, in which 873 people left the aircraft within the required 90 seconds using half of the 16 doors. The test was supervised by EASA and the FAA, and one passenger broke a leg.
XIaovi1JWyY.why: Cited in threads about evacuation rules, mostly as an example of a certification test that commenters call unrealistic.

XLzBMGXfK4c.summary: Michael Jordan's 2009 Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame enshrinement speech, in which he thanks and also airs grievances about people who doubted him. It is known for his stories of using slights as motivation.
XLzBMGXfK4c.why: HN refers to it as a source for Jordan's motivation-from-slights anecdotes and his cut-from-the-team story.

XPGgTy5YJ-g.summary: A clip from Futurama's 'A Fistful of Dollars' where Fry and Leela discuss ads appearing in dreams. It satirizes advertising creeping into every part of life.
XPGgTy5YJ-g.why: Posted as a joke or reference whenever a product starts showing more ads.

XQLdhVpLBVE.summary: An Adult Swim parody infomercial for a for-profit online university that promises to let you print your own degree. It is absurdist comedy in the style of Tim and Eric.
XQLdhVpLBVE.why: Mentioned as a joke when threads touch on credentials, degrees or scams.

XQQYbKT_rMg.summary: A short Star Trek: The Next Generation clip about how money no longer exists in the 24th century. It shows the crew explaining a post-scarcity economy to people from the 20th century.
XQQYbKT_rMg.why: HN commenters link it to illustrate Star Trek's moneyless economy in discussions of post-scarcity and the future.

XR9d4ESlpHY.summary: A clip of "My Pal Foot Foot" by The Shaggs, the 1960s sisters band famous for their off-kilter amateur sound. The uploader credits a Frank Zappa quote claiming they are better than the Beatles.
XR9d4ESlpHY.why: HN links it as the canonical example of music considered terrible, usually with affection or as a joke.

XWPCE2tTLZQ.summary: A very short clip of George Carlin's bit on idiots and maniacs, about the other drivers on the road.
XWPCE2tTLZQ.why: HN uses it only as a joke reference when talking about bad drivers or poor code.

XYcxvEfUikg.summary: A short clip from MIX08 in which Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer grabs Guy Kawasaki's MacBook Air from its envelope during a Q&A and mocks it.
XYcxvEfUikg.why: HN uses it as a recurring example of Microsoft leadership dismissing a product that later proved significant.

XZmGGAbHqa0.summary: Joe Kava, VP of Google's Data Center Operations, gives a short tour of a Google data center. He covers security, sustainability and the core infrastructure architecture.
XZmGGAbHqa0.why: Cited as a documentary look at how Google runs its data centers, though sometimes dismissed as PR.

X_8E3ENrKrQ.summary: A short audio clip of a 1981 interview in which Republican strategist Lee Atwater explains to a political scientist how the party could win racist voters without using overtly racist language. It was published by The Nation with analysis by Rick Perlstein.
X_8E3ENrKrQ.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for the Southern Strategy and coded racial language, in Atwater's own words.

XaGHcBZjmWA.summary: Louis Rossmann examines a 2012 MacBook Pro logic board that Apple refurbished for GPU failures and that failed again. He criticizes the quality of Apple's authorized repair work and argues for right to repair.
XaGHcBZjmWA.why: Cited in threads about Apple repair and refurbishment as evidence of poor refurbishing, with a warning that Rossmann uses colorful language.

Xa_fNuaSE_I.summary: The Browser Company's CTO explains how the team is building the Arc browser for Windows using Swift. It covers the de-risking work and why they believe it is feasible.
Xa_fNuaSE_I.why: Used mainly as evidence that Swift is being used for a real Windows application.

XamC7-Pt8N0.summary: A movie clip from The Gambler (2014) in which John Goodman's character explains to Mark Wahlberg's the idea of having enough money to tell anyone to go to hell. The relevant part is the first 45 seconds.
XamC7-Pt8N0.why: Linked in career and burnout threads as shorthand for the freedom financial independence gives you.

XbZ8zDpX2Mg.summary: A one-minute joke video titled as a warning against buying Bitcoin, giving a humorous summary of price crashes. It has no description.
XbZ8zDpX2Mg.why: Posted as a recurring joke every time Bitcoin's price crashes or hits headlines.

XduK7wn9SE4.summary: A demo of the Bad Apple music video played back at 60 FPS on an e-ink display, up from 2.4 FPS in an earlier attempt. It is part of the effort behind the open source Modos e-ink monitor.
XduK7wn9SE4.why: HN cites it as the demonstration that e-ink can do low-latency, video-rate refresh with an open hardware controller.

Xe1TZaElTAs.summary: A short Supernova 2007 provocation in which Clay Shirky uses a 1300-year-old Japanese shrine, rebuilt periodically, as a metaphor for how networks change business and collective creativity.
Xe1TZaElTAs.why: HN people cite it for the Ise shrine metaphor, that function rather than original material defines identity.

XeIIpLqsOe4.summary: A short Charlie Rose interview clip of Eric Schmidt discussing Google's direction for search. It is remembered for his remark that returning more than one result is a bug.
XeIIpLqsOe4.why: Quoted, often critically, to argue that Google aims for a single answer and to compare it with ChatGPT-style answers.

XewVicFzRxw.summary: A sketch from A Bit of Fry and Laurie, season 1 episode 4, featuring a 'Doctor Tobacco' routine.
XewVicFzRxw.why: Posted as a comedic reference in threads on salt, abstraction, or cigarette ads.

XfonhlM6I7w.summary: A look at Le Plessis-Robinson, a French suburb transformed from modernist urbanism into traditional mixed-use fabric with local-style architecture, green space and a more balanced housing supply.
XfonhlM6I7w.why: HN cites it in housing and urbanism threads as an example of a dense, beautiful neighbourhood built in recent times.

XggxeuFDaDU.summary: Short British Pathe newsreel footage of the 1940 collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge as it twisted and swayed in the wind. The only casualty was a dog left in a stalled car.
XggxeuFDaDU.why: HN uses the footage as a visual illustration of resonance and oscillation growing until structural failure.

XiQkeWOFwmk.summary: A one-minute Tesla clip showing multiple Tesla-built Optimus bots walking and learning about the real world.
XiQkeWOFwmk.why: Referenced as evidence of Tesla's humanoid robot progress and its data collection efforts.

XpunFFS-n8I.summary: A Netflix engineer describes how Netflix uses Java in 2025, including Spring Boot, DGS/GraphQL, gRPC and keeping over 3000 services on the latest JDK. It covers generational ZGC upgrade experiences.
XpunFFS-n8I.why: Cited as a real-world enterprise Java example, especially for JDK upgrades and ZGC results.

XqZsoesa55w.summary: The Pinkfong Baby Shark Dance children's song video, one of the most viewed videos on YouTube.
XqZsoesa55w.why: Mentioned mainly as a statistic or joke about being the most watched video in history.

XrlrbfGZo2k.summary: A 37C3 talk on how a series of Polish electric trains stopped working after servicing by an independent company. The speakers explain how train control systems work and how they reverse-engineered the software lockouts.
XrlrbfGZo2k.why: HN cites it as the key account of train DRM being broken, in threads on right to repair, reverse engineering and vendor lockouts.

Xv2VIEY9-A8.summary: The classic SNL sketch in which motivational speaker Matt Foley, played by Chris Farley, warns teens they will end up living in a van down by the river.
Xv2VIEY9-A8.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke in threads about vans, van life or career failure.

XxbJw8PrIkc.summary: A short extended clip of Steve Ballmer sweating and chanting "developers" on stage at a .NET presentation around 1999 or 2000.
XxbJw8PrIkc.why: HN references it as a meme about Ballmer's famous energy, in jokes and in threads about high-energy people.

Xybzyv8qbOc.summary: Christian Thalinger presents at the 2015 JVM Language Summit on adding ahead-of-time compilation to the JVM, covering the HotSpot team's AOT work and its relation to warmup and deoptimization.
Xybzyv8qbOc.why: Cited in AOT discussions as evidence that Oracle was moving toward AOT in the JDK and as an explanation of the deoptimization concerns.
